reason: The skin cell needs to copy its DNA before it can divide and renew the skin.
expectation: The cell will replicate its chromosomes in preparation for division.

effect: The chromosomes are copied and ready to be separated as the skin cell divides.
reaction: The before-and-after description makes the copying step clear.
reason: The copied chromosomes need to be separated before the cell can divide.
expectation: The machinery will separate the copied chromosomes toward opposite sides of the cell.

effect: The chromosome sets are now at opposite poles, but the cell still has one shared interior.
reaction: The description clearly distinguishes chromosome separation from cell division.
reason: The division ring can divide the cell after its chromosomes have separated.

choice.combine: Skin cell with separated chromosome sets

expectation: The ring will constrict to form two skin cells, each with a complete chromosome set.

effect: The skin cell has divided into two daughter cells, providing cells that can renew the skin surface.
reaction: The tightening ring makes the final division step clear.
reason: Erythropoietin is shown carrying a kidney signal to marrow, where the red-cell precursors are located.
expectation: The signal will stimulate the precursors to produce new red blood cells.

effect: The kidney signal has started red-cell development in the marrow.
reaction: The low-oxygen cue gives the signal a clear purpose.
reason: Bone-removing and bone-forming cells are shown working on the same patch of bone, so they appear to be the next pair for renewal.
expectation: They will show old bone being removed and new matrix deposited in its place.

effect: The bone-removing cells cannot be combined directly with the bone-forming cells, so I need another route for bone renewal.
reaction: I expected them to work together, so the result was surprising.
reason: The new skin cells belong to the same body and may advance the renewal goal.
expectation: The new cells will be incorporated into the body's renewing skin.

alternatives.reason: The bone-removing cells may need to act on bone in the body first.

effect: The new skin cells are incorporated into the body, showing renewal alongside surface shedding.
reaction: The connection to the whole body makes the earlier division steps feel purposeful.
reason: The developing red cells can now be connected to the same body to continue blood renewal.
expectation: The developing cells will mature and contribute new red blood cells to the body.

alternatives.reason: The bone-removing cells may need to act on the body's bone first.

effect: The body now shows both skin renewal and new red cells entering the blood.
reaction: The kidney-to-marrow connection gives blood renewal a clear purpose.
reason: Bone-removing cells could not combine directly with bone-forming cells, so I’ll try applying them to the body’s bone first.
expectation: The cells will remove a patch of old bone matrix as the first stage of bone renewal.

effect: Old bone is being removed in the same body, leaving a patch for new matrix.
reaction: Applying the removing cells to the body first makes the sequence clearer.
reason: The bone-forming cells are shown depositing matrix in the hollow left by bone removal.
expectation: The cells will deposit new bone matrix in the patch and complete the bone-renewal sequence.

effect: Bone-forming cells rebuilt the patch, completing the goal and connecting skin, blood and bone renewal in the same body.
reaction: Seeing the three renewal processes brought together made the sequence feel complete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Dividing the skin cell was most worthwhile: the chromosome separation and tightening ring made it clear how two cells can each receive a complete set.

leastWorthwhile.text: The direct attempt to combine bone-removing and bone-forming cells was least worthwhile. The pictures suggested they worked on the same patch, but the feedback did not explain why they could not combine directly.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the bone-removing cells first had to act on the body rather than combine with the bone-forming cells.

arbitrary.text: The required ordering for bone renewal was initially unclear, although applying the cells to the body made sense once it worked.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it offered a similarly clear connection between cellular work and the whole body, though the mostly sequential combinations might become repetitive.
